title: FlashLoop: Fast and Memory-Efficient Looped Transformers via Lazy Updates
summary: FlashLoop replaces full per-loop recomputation and full KV caching in Looped Transformers with token-sparse updates, sparse attention over dominant key columns, and low-bit quantization of KV residuals between adjacent loops. It is training-free, so the cost is implementation complexity in the inference path plus reliance on the empirical observation that cross-loop state changes concentrate on a small, stable token subset. It can fail when that sparsity assumption does not hold for a given model, loop depth, or context length, degrading accuracy or negating the savings, and it applies only if the reader actually deploys Looped Transformers rather than standard architectures.
rationale: The method is training-free and fits a single 24 GB GPU, but its benefits are contingent on using Looped Transformer models and on workload-specific sparsity, so it warrants small-scale validation before production adoption.
technique: Lazy cross-loop updates for Looped Transformers

It is training-free, so the cost is implementation complexity in the inference path plus reliance on the empirical observation that cross-loop state changes concentrate on a small, stable token subset. It can fail when that sparsity assumption does not hold for a given model, loop depth, or context length, degrading accuracy or negating the savings, and it applies only if the reader actually deploys Looped Transformers rather than standard architectures.
Lossless accuracy with up to 1.64x end-to-end speedup and up to 6x KV-cache memory reduction across several Looped Transformer models.
